previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 16th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with only mild nausea, managed with anti-emetics. Methotrexate levels cleared appropriately, reaching below 0.2 by discharge, with no renal toxicity. Liver enzymes showed mild, expected elevation. An MRI confirmed stable lymphoma without new lesions. Due to a recent ulcerative colitis flare with hematochezia, oral mesalamine was switched to rectal suppositories to avoid interference with methotrexate excretion. Aspirin was held during admission for the same reason and was restarted at discharge. She remained emotionally stable, denied depression or suicidal ideation, and was discharged home in good condition with follow-up instructions.

# CNS lymphoma: Restaging brain MRI ___ stable.  Given ___ 
cycle #17 high-dose MTX 8g/m2.  24hr creatinine clearance 
205mL/min (83mL/min last cycle).  Alkalinization with sodium 
bicarbonate PO and IV fluids to enhance methotrexate excretion.  
Leucovorin rescue to start 24hrs after MTX given.  Followed MTX 
levels daily starting 24hrs after MTX given.  Home when MTX 
<0.20.  Anti-emetics pre-meds and PRN.  Repeat 24hr creatinine 
clearance with next cycle.  She tolerated this cycle very well.  
MTX level at discharge was <0.1, so did not need to take any 
extra leucovorin or sodium bicarbonate.
.

Colonoscopy ___ at ___ showed mild proctitis 
with the rest of colon normal.  PO mesalamine was switch to PR 
mesalamine and her hematochezia cleared in a couple days.  She
